newsitem.title: USA: Clinton announces strong new U.S. clean air rules.
newsitem.headline: Clinton announces strong new U.S. clean air rules.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday he had approved strong new clean air standards to reduce pollution and protect public health.
"I approved some very strong new regulations today that will be somewhat controversial. But I think kids ought to be healthy," Clinton told a conference on family values.

Clinton made the announcement just one day before he was to address a U.N. summit on the environment in New York, where the United States has been criticized for not doing enough to protect the environment.
The proposals by the Environmental Protection Agency would set tough new standards for soot and smog.

"We think if we have high standards for protecting the environment, but we're flexible in how those standards are implemented...that we can protect the environment and grow the economy," Clinton said.

EPA's proposal last November sparked a major controversy, with U.S. industry groups and some cities and states saying that controls needed to meet the new standards would be far too costly, and environmental and health advocates saying existing standards were too weak to protect children from lung diseases.
